summary: Formats/Latest (Revit 2026 archive class map, 496,597 B, sha256 6459a9a9…, identical in all six files, re-verified) is now fully decoded. The wave-1 schema-a grammar was correct; over the corrected de-paged stream it needed exactly ONE extension: the descriptor's u16 third word ('extra') is not always 0 (single exception VarExpr.m_refCt = 0x0004), plus an 8-byte all-zero EOF sentinel. Result: parse reaches EOF with ZERO gaps and ZERO unresolved backward refs. Canonical module src/rvt/schema.py (load_schema() -> Schema with by_id/by_name, fields with name/kind/flags/type_id/type_name/count/element, parent links, guids) emits schema.json (4,690 classes), type_ids.json, mep_classes.txt (407 electrical/MEP classes). Id model = definition order + 0x0c with NO drift: 16/16 anchors match (12 exact names, 2 exact-family AString->AStringWrapper and DocumentStorageIndex->Impl, 2 where the wave-1 guessed label named the sibling class at a correct ordinal). rvt-rs's 'tag' column is proven to be the inline-defined base class's id = our id+1 (60/60). Kind codebook corrected by ground truth from 394 std::pair<> synthetic classes (0x02=char, 0x03=short, contradicting rvt-rs). docs/streams/01-schema.md rewritten as the canonical spec; 01-schema-a/b.md and schema_a/b.py untouched.
key_findings: Full parse to EOF: 496,589 bytes consumed + 8-byte zero EOF sentinel = 496,597; 0 unparsed gaps; 0 unresolved backward type-refs; identical results on all six files (4,690 classes, 12,558 fields each).

4,690 classes (3,604 top-level ASCII-sorted class records + 1,086 inline definitions), 12,558 fields, 1,677 per-class GUID entries (ADocument holds 1,509), type ids 0x000c–0x125d. ZDI counted 4,611 for Revit 2025; 2026 has 4,690.

Only two grammar deltas past the old 138 KB frontier: descriptor bytes 2-3 ('extra' u16) is nonzero exactly once (VarExpr.m_refCt = kind 0x04 extra 0x0004 at 0x72d3d, framing unaffected) and the stream ends with an 8-byte zero sentinel after 'testclass'. New flag values 0x04/0x13/0x53/0x54 appear (var-pointer/weak flavours) but follow existing framing rules.

Id model = definition order (top-level and inline share one counter) + 0x0c with NO ±1 drift. Anchor validation 16/16: 0x1c ADocument, 0x14 ElementId, 0x1f AStringWrapper (=AString), 0x25 Element, 0x5c9 ElemTable, 0x538 DocumentHistory, 0x53c DocumentIncrementTable, 0x53e DocumentStorageIndexImpl (Contents), 0xc80 PartitionTable, 0x5e5 ElementHeader, 0xf2c SerializedDummy, 0x89e GElement, 0x8cc GStyleElem, 0x2e1 CategoryElem all exact; 0x3a2/0x3a3 are ContentKey/ContentMarker (true ContentRec = 0x3a4) — the wave-1 guessed names, not the ordinals, were one slot off.

Top-level class records are stored in strict ASCII byte order of class name (0 descents across 3,604) — the schema is a sorted class registry; id = sorted rank + count of preceding inline definitions.

rvt-rs's per-class 'serialization tag' is actually the inline-defined base class's id: their 2026 tag == our id + 1 for all 60 comparable classes (0 exceptions). Their 400-class/64 KB cap and 'binary noise' belief are the paging artefact.

Kind codebook ground truth from 394 std::pair<A,B> synthetic classes: 0x01 bool, 0x02 char (byte), 0x03 short, 0x04 int, 0x05 uint, 0x06 float, 0x07 double, 0x08 AString (flags 0x60), 0x09 GUID, 0x0a classref, 0x0b int64, 0x0d inline-array, 0x0e class-ref. This corrects rvt-rs (0x02=u16, 0x03=deprecated i32) and schema-a (0x03=uint16).
Element (0x25) has 895 total descendants (383 direct); max inheritance depth 7 (RbsDuctInsulation ... > HostObj > Element). Most-referenced types: ElementId 2,100, XYZ 218, GUIDvalue 94, Trf 82.

407 electrical/MEP classes exported; key ones: 0x596 ElectricalCircuit (Element; fields incl. m_idPanel, m_dRating, m_dVoltageDrop, m_nPoles, m_nStartSlot), 0x5a4 ElectricalLoadClassification, 0x5ae ElectricalSetting, 0x381 ConnectorElem, 0x37e ConnectorDomainElectrical, 0x2b6 CableTray, 0xb48 PanelScheduleView (TableView>DBView>Element), 0xb41 PanelScheduleData.
